Category: "Non-automatic weighing instrument" — schema says category examples like "Load cell", "Indicator"... For this, category should be "Non-automatic weighing instrument".

Module designation: Not applicable (weighing instrument — complete instrument). Actually schema says "Analog load cell" | "Not applicable" | null. For a complete NAWI, "Not applicable" seems right. But don't fabricate — the cert doesn't mention module designation. Hmm. The rule 8 says don't fabricate if not present. The category is mentioned. Module designation is not present. I could omit or set null. Safer: omit or null. I'll set "Not applicable"? The schema allows null. I'll just omit it or set null. Actually let me set it to null? Including a null field is fine per schema. I'll omit to be safe... The schema lists module_designation in certified_type. I'll include "module_designation": null? Rule 8: if a field is not present, omit it. So omit.

Description: "A Non-automatic weighing instrument" — could include.

Model family: The cert covers two models: BI-10000 Helios and BI-10000 Atoll. Characteristics: Max range 2.5-15 kg, e ≥ 2g, n ≤ 3000, T ≤ -Max, temperature -10/+40 °C. No per-model variation given, so model_family: include only if cert covers >1 model variant. Two type designations — two variants. Include models [{"model_id": "BI-10000 Helios"}, {"model_id": "BI-10000 Atoll"}]. family_name: "BI-10000"? The family could be "BI-10000" with variants Helios and Atoll. That seems reasonable. family_name: "BI-10000", models: [{"model_id": "BI-10000 Helios", "label": "Helios"}, {"model_id": "BI-10000 Atoll", "label": "Atoll"}]. Hmm, don't over-fabricate. I'll use model_id as full designations.

Characteristics type_level:
- maximum_capacity: 2.5 kg ≤ Max ≤ 15 kg → value {min: 2.5, max: 15}, unit kg
- verification_scale_interval / scale interval e: e ≥ 2 g → {min: 2, max: null}, unit g
- number_of_verification_scale_intervals: n ≤ 3000 divisions → {min: null, max: 3000}, unit "divisions"
- tare: T ≤ - Max → this is a formula. value "T ≤ -Max" → attribute tare_capacity, value "-Max" string. Actually "T ≤ - Max" means tare ≤ -Max (i.e., subtractive tare up to Max). Value: string "-Max"? Keep as string "-Max". Hmm, the structured value: {"value": "-Max", "unit_symbol": "kg", ...}. Actually T ≤ -Max: value = "-Max" with unit kg. I'll record attribute "tare" with value "-Max" (string), unit "kg".

- temperature_range: {min: -10, max: 40}, unit "°C"

Recommendation: R76, edition 2006, accuracy_classes ["III"], scheme: "A"? OIML-CS scheme A vs B: Certificates of conformity under the OIML Certification System... Scheme A is the standard OIML Certificate of Conformity (Issuing Authority issues certificate based on test report). Scheme B involves... Actually in OIML-CS, "OIML Certificate" is issued under Scheme A. Scheme B is for MAA (Mutual Acceptance Arrangement) — "OIML Certificate MAA" issued by an Issuing Authority under the MAA. This is a 2012 certificate, pre-MAA? MAA started around 2011-2012 for R76? NMi Certin as NL1 issuing authority... This cert is a regular OIML Certificate of Conformity (not MAA). Scheme A.

Canonical id "R76", edition 2006 (int), amendment null, scheme "A", accuracy_classes ["III"].

Test reports:
- R76/1992-NL1-03.61A, 18 pages, role type_evaluation_report? These are OIML test reports. Role: "test_report" for all, or "type_evaluation_report". The text: "results of tests and examinations provided in the associated OIML Test Report(s)". Role: test_report. Ids: "R76/1992-NL1-03.61A" pages 18; "R76/1992-NL1-03.61B" 56; "R76/1992-NL1-04.24A" 36; "R76/1992-NL1-04.24B" 28; "R76/1992-NL1-07.14" 34; "NMi-11200063-02" 26. Dates not given.

Revision history: none.

Footnotes: none.

Matrix tables: none.

Components: none.

Units: "u:kilogram", "u:gram", "u:degree_Celsius" — the rule says leave unit_id null unless certain of the unitsdb ID. The examples in schema show "u:degree_Celsius" as valid format. I'm fairly confident about u:kilogram, u:gram, u:degree_Celsius in unitsdb. These are the standard UCUM-style codes used in unitsdb (quantities.unitsdb.org). Yes: u:kilogram, u:gram, u:degree_Celsius exist. I'll include them. For divisions, null. For tare with "-Max" value, unit kg.

Wait — tare: "T ≤ - Max". Keep as string "-Max"? The convention: value "-Max" meaning negative of Max. I'll keep value: "-Max". Attribute name: "tare" or "maximum_tare_effect". I'll use "tare" with value "-Max" (string formula). Or omit? It's a characteristic mentioned; better to record.

Actually maybe better: "maximum_tare_effect": {"value": "≤ -Max"...} — no, keep value "-Max" as formula string. Fine.
